data.title: What Cenovus Energy Shareholders Got Right
data.description:
If you only skimmed the Q3 2026 headlines about Cenovus Energy’s record production and much fatter net margin, you might assume the share price had quietly tracked that operational step up all year. For Cenovus Energy shareholders, the return over the past year was 56.9%, including dividends. If that outcome hinged on acquisitions, dividend moves and shifting analyst views that were not guaranteed in late 2025, what exactly was knowable when the decision window opened?

Cenovus Energy has already moved. See which of 2 high quality undervalued stocks still trade below our estimates.

The Two Cenovus Energy Stories Investors Had To Weigh

The shares cost CA$25.68 at the start of the period, and Cenovus Energy investors were effectively choosing between two plausible stories about where the business could go next.

The bullish case saw Cenovus Energy as a project completion and optimization story, with a fair value of CA$27.67, a price implied by assumptions such as 4.1% annual revenue growth and profit margins reaching 6.5% over three years.

The more cautious view focused on deal execution risk, with a fair value of CA$24, based on a 9.1% revenue growth assumption alongside a 5.7% margin and a future P/E of 11.8x.

What The Results Changed For The Cenovus Energy Thesis

The key fact is what Cenovus Energy actually produced in Q3 2026. Revenue was C$15,984m and net income reached C$3,360m, up from C$13,195m and C$1,284m a year earlier, with net margin moving from 9.7% to 21.0%. That profitability outcome leaned toward the bullish case, while ongoing acquisition integration kept the cautious story alive. Overall, the evidence cut both ways.

The useful takeaway is simple. When a thesis hinges on better margins, track the reported net margin against the original forecast and ask whether acquisitions are lifting it or simply adding scale with extra risk attached.

What Cenovus Energy’s Run Now Prices In

Cenovus Energy now trades at CA$39 after rising 56.9% over the past year, and the analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St places its Fair Value above that level based on current assumptions.

That Narrative focuses on integrated oil sands and refining assets and states that today’s price still does not fully credit successful thermal growth and acquisition integration.

Cenovus And The Pipes Beside It

Cenovus gives you production and refining scale. One step away sits the plumbing that keeps oil and gas moving.

This other business focuses on transporting and storing hydrocarbons and power, mostly on fee based terms. Your barrels and molecules need dependable routes, not just well run fields.

Its plans lean on new pipelines, gas storage and related projects. These assets aim to provide more contracted cash flow over longer periods.

Execution and funding choices will decide how useful that expansion becomes. If the projects work as intended, the role in the energy system could feel very different.

data.title: US Stock Market Today: S&P 500 Futures Slip As Higher Rate Fears Resurface
data.description:
The Morning Bull - US Market Morning Update Friday, Nov, 20 2026

US stocks look set to open weaker, with S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures in the red as investors refocus on the Federal Reserve. The dominant driver is a renewed push toward higher US rates after hawkish Fed minutes.

Minutes from the October meeting showed most Fed officials leaning toward additional tightening, and markets now price roughly a 25bp hike next month with a smaller possibility of 50bp. The US 10 year yield sits near 5.05% after a four session slide, while the dollar index is pushing toward 104, reflecting that higher rate expectation.

Higher policy expectations keep borrowing costs elevated for households and companies, which can pressure capital spending plans and squeeze interest sensitive business models. A stronger dollar also tightens financial conditions by making US exports less competitive and compressing overseas earnings when they are translated back into US$.

The open question is how long the Fed can lean hawkish without triggering a sharper growth scare. Today’s focus is on upcoming Fed speeches, which could either reinforce the case for another hike or hint at more patience instead.

Stocks to Watch Before the Opening Bell

Merck (MRK)

Fresh data from Merck's Phase 3 TroFuse-015 trial is front and center. Its drug sacituzumab tirumotecan met the primary goal of improving overall survival in heavily pretreated gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma. The therapy is a TROP2-directed antibody drug conjugate with a safety profile in line with earlier work. Investors now watch for regulatory filings and how Merck positions this within its oncology lineup.

General Dynamics (GD)

General Dynamics is juggling wins and setbacks in government contracting. The group secured a US Army deal worth up to US$333m over five years for Stryker vehicle sustainment, plus a place in a US$7.13b Navy electronic warfare program shared among 28 contractors. At the same time, it lost a challenge over a separate US$10.5b Special Operations logistics award to Lockheed Martin.

Anthropic PBC (ANT)

Anthropic PBC is in focus after Purpose Investments launched the Purpose Anthropic Yield Shares ETF in Canada. The product uses a covered call approach that targets monthly income while keeping exposure to Anthropic. The ETF gives investors another route into the AI theme without buying single equity directly. Attention now turns to trading volumes and how closely the fund tracks the underlying shares.

Top Movers

  • Insmed (INSM) jumped 20.58% after reports that Sanofi is exploring a potential takeover of the biotech group.
  • PDD Holdings (PDD) advanced 11.04% as Q3 earnings beat expectations and multiple broker upgrades followed the profit surprise.
  • Palo Alto Networks (PANW) gained 6.42% following a strong Q1 beat, raised FY2027 guidance and a US$4.5b Applied Compute acquisition.

Top Losers

  • Williams-Sonoma (WSM) fell 15.16% after Q3 earnings beat, as analysts cut price targets following high expectations and softer comps.
  • Zoom Communications (ZM) declined 9.56%.
  • Nebius Group (NBIS) declined 9.39% as neocloud and AI stocks extended a selloff on funding and demand concerns.

On The Radar

US traders head into the next few sessions with Fed messaging, inflation gauges and a heavy tech and retail earnings slate doing most of the work on rate expectations and sector positioning.

  • Fed Waller speech, Fri 20 Nov. Any push for more tightening after the October minutes already flagged a possible 25bp move would keep pressure on rate sensitive areas like housing and utilities and support the stronger dollar story.
  • Michigan Consumer Sentiment Final, Fri 20 Nov. A reading above the 51.5 consensus would point to a firmer US consumer than the prior 48.0 print suggested and help support discretionary stocks into the holiday period, while a softer figure would do the opposite.
  • Best Buy, Tue 24 Nov. Q3 2027 numbers put the spotlight on comparable sales and gross margin in core electronics, which shows how higher financing costs and promotional activity are feeding through to big ticket spending.
  • Dell Technologies, Tue 24 Nov. Q3 2027 results will hinge on infrastructure and PC revenue and on margin commentary that shows how the group is handling component costs and a firm US dollar in its global orders.
  • Core PCE Price Index MoM, Wed 25 Nov. An October reading above the 0.3% forecast would reinforce the case for more Fed tightening and support higher Treasury yields, while a softer print would ease some pressure across growth stocks.

Sector & Industry Watch

Tech: Fed nerves hit high-growth stories

Tech has retreated over the past week, with a weaker 7 day return than the broader US Market after the Fed minutes pushed rate expectations higher and lifted the dollar. AI headlines around Anthropic, Microsoft and others have not offset that drag, since higher borrowing costs reduce what investors are willing to pay for future profits from cloud, software and data centers.

If you hold broad tech ETFs, the clearest near term swing factor is today’s Fed Waller speech. Any firm push for more tightening would keep pressure on valuations, even if AI earnings commentary stays upbeat.

Semiconductors: AI chips squeezed by policy worries

Semiconductors are having a tougher week than Tech overall, with the 7 day return weaker again as export control stories, the AMD short seller report and talk around Nvidia’s China exposure all weigh on sentiment. Strong news like Intel’s chip breakthrough and new AI related wins at Teradyne and Microchip sits alongside concern about tighter rules on advanced processors headed to Chinese firms.

For anyone in chip ETFs or AI hardware stocks, the single catalyst to watch is Washington’s next move on export controls to China. A stricter framework would matter for revenue mix at several US chipmakers and could keep this industry more volatile than broader Tech.

Energy & Oil and Gas: Softer crude after strong 12 month run

Energy and Oil and Gas are down over the past 7 days and 30 days even though both sectors still show gains of roughly 32% to 33% over 12 months. Crude holding near a three month low after a US inventory build is feeding into that short term pullback, while deals at TechnipFMC and Cheniere underline how producers keep investing carefully when pricing cools.

If your portfolio includes US producers or LNG linked stocks, weekly US petroleum inventory data is the key dial now. Bigger builds can keep questions alive about demand and leave Energy lagging rate sensitive areas like Tech and Real Estate.

Metals and Mining: Copper and rare earth stories under pressure

Metals and Mining is one of the weakest groups this week, with the sector’s 7 day return down about 12.4% and slightly negative year to date despite a positive 1 year figure. News around Freeport McMoRan’s Indonesia operations, new US rare earth processing plans and antimony supply efforts shows plenty happening on the ground, yet the stronger dollar and recent copper price drop are still weighing on listed miners.

If you hold diversified mining or copper focused ETFs, the variable to track is the US dollar trend. A firm dollar can keep pressure on commodity sectors even when individual project updates, such as new US copper finds, look constructive.

Healthcare & Pharmaceuticals & Biotech: Drug pipelines vs short term swings

Healthcare and Pharmaceuticals & Biotech have both eased over the last 7 days, while their 12 month returns still sit ahead of the US Market helped by strong past earnings and active pipelines. Fresh trial and approval news from Merck, Regeneron, Bristol Myers Squibb and others keeps attention on product data rather than day to day macro headlines.

If you rely on Healthcare as a steadier part of your portfolio, the main US catalyst in view is today’s Michigan Consumer Sentiment reading. A weaker consumer backdrop can keep interest in sectors with more predictable cash flows, which often includes large pharma alongside Consumer Staples and Utilities.

data.title: What Adobe Doubters Saw Before The Drop
data.description:
Adobe has had a packed year, from record quarterly revenue to a sweeping leadership handover and a huge new buyback plan, all while AI-first tools like Firefly reworked how creatives use its software. Holding Adobe from the start of the year would have meant a 33.5% loss, including dividends. If you had made that call on 1 January, how much of today’s debate about freemium AI, margins and user growth would you be expecting management to answer next?

This theme extends beyond Adobe. See which of 42 AI small caps may still merit a closer look.

The Two Adobe Stories Investors Had To Weigh

The shares cost US$350 at the start of the period, and you were choosing between two very different stories about what Adobe’s AI push might deliver.

On the upbeat side, the Firefly and GenStudio narrative pointed to a Fair Value of US$456, a theoretical price implied by assumptions such as revenue growth of 8.8% and a 29.2% profit margin supported by deeper enterprise integration.

The more cautious view saw Firefly and AI assistants still drawing new users but assigned a Fair Value of US$280, with concerns that execution risks and pressure on revenue and margins could weigh on the business.

What The Adobe Evidence Actually Tested

Adobe’s record Q3 2026 revenue of US$6.76b and higher net income supported the upbeat case that Firefly, GenStudio and AI-first products could lift the top line. The drop in net margin from 29.6% to 27.0%, together with concerns about freemium AI pressure on revenue and profitability, kept the cautious view alive. Overall, the evidence cut both ways.

The episode turned on one assumption: higher AI usage had to show up not just in revenue, but in stable or improving profitability. For any other software stock, track the combination of ARR growth, reported net margin and how management explains freemium or AI giveaways in earnings calls.

What Adobe’s Share Price Drop Is Asking You To Believe

Adobe trades at US$222 from the start of the year, with the share price down 33.5%. This Narrative’s Fair Value sits above the current price, which according to BlackJesus, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community who wrote the Narrative, reflects a market that has leaned heavily into AI fear.

The argument hinges on Adobe’s role in professional, brand-safe workflows rather than casual content. For the Narrative’s higher figure to be reached, buyers today would need to assume Firefly and related tools convert enterprise AI usage into durable, paid subscription and credit demand.

data.title: There's A Lot To Like About Build-A-Bear Workshop's (NYSE:BBW) Upcoming US$0.23 Dividend
data.description:
Some investors rely on dividends for growing their wealth, and if you're one of those dividend sleuths, you might be intrigued to know that Build-A-Bear Workshop, Inc. (NYSE:BBW) is about to go ex-dividend in just four days. The ex-dividend date is one business day before the record date, which is the cut-off date for shareholders to be present on the company's books to be eligible for a dividend payment. The ex-dividend date is an important date to be aware of as any purchase of the stock made on or after this date might mean a late settlement that doesn't show on the record date. Therefore, if you purchase Build-A-Bear Workshop's shares on or after the 25th of November, you won't be eligible to receive the dividend, when it is paid on the 7th of January.

The company's next dividend payment will be US$0.23 per share, and in the last 12 months, the company paid a total of US$0.92 per share. Based on the last year's worth of payments, Build-A-Bear Workshop has a trailing yield of 3.2% on the current stock price of US$28.87. If you buy this business for its dividend, you should have an idea of whether Build-A-Bear Workshop's dividend is reliable and sustainable. We need to see whether the dividend is covered by earnings and if it's growing.

We've found 21 US stocks that are forecast to pay a dividend yield of over 6% next year. See the full list for free.

Dividends are typically paid from company earnings. If a company pays more in dividends than it earned in profit, then the dividend could be unsustainable. Build-A-Bear Workshop is paying out just 22% of its profit after tax, which is comfortably low and leaves plenty of breathing room in the case of adverse events. That said, even highly profitable companies sometimes might not generate enough cash to pay the dividend, which is why we should always check if the dividend is covered by cash flow. Fortunately, it paid out only 47% of its free cash flow in the past year.

data.title: eGain's (NASDAQ:EGAN) Conservative Accounting Might Explain Soft Earnings
data.description:

We've found 21 US stocks that are forecast to pay a dividend yield of over 6% next year. See the full list for free.

Zooming In On eGain's Earnings

In high finance, the key ratio used to measure how well a company converts reported profits into free cash flow (FCF) is the accrual ratio (from cashflow). In plain english, this ratio subtracts FCF from net profit, and divides that number by the company's average operating assets over that period. The ratio shows us how much a company's profit exceeds its FCF.

That means a negative accrual ratio is a good thing, because it shows that the company is bringing in more free cash flow than its profit would suggest. That is not intended to imply we should worry about a positive accrual ratio, but it's worth noting where the accrual ratio is rather high. Notably, there is some academic evidence that suggests that a high accrual ratio is a bad sign for near-term profits, generally speaking.

Over the twelve months to September 2026, eGain recorded an accrual ratio of -0.37. Therefore, its statutory earnings were very significantly less than its free cashflow. To wit, it produced free cash flow of US$12m during the period, dwarfing its reported profit of US$7.61m. eGain did see its free cash flow drop year on year, which is less than ideal, like a Simpson's episode without Groundskeeper Willie.

data.title: News Flash: 7 Analysts Think Crescent Biopharma, Inc. (NASDAQ:CBIO) Earnings Are Under Threat
data.description:
The latest analyst coverage could presage a bad day for Crescent Biopharma, Inc. (NASDAQ:CBIO), with the analysts making across-the-board cuts to their statutory estimates that might leave shareholders a little shell-shocked. Both revenue and earnings per share (EPS) forecasts went under the knife, suggesting analysts have soured majorly on the business.

Following the latest downgrade, the current consensus, from the seven analysts covering Crescent Biopharma, is for revenues of US$3.4m in 2027, which would reflect a painful 78% reduction in Crescent Biopharma's sales over the past 12 months. Losses are presumed to reduce, shrinking 15% per share from last year to US$3.54. Yet before this consensus update, the analysts had been forecasting revenues of US$4.8m and losses of US$3.06 per share in 2027. So there's been quite a change-up of views after the recent consensus updates, with the analysts making a serious cut to their revenue forecasts while also expecting losses per share to increase.

See our latest analysis for Crescent Biopharma

Looking at the bigger picture now, one of the ways we can make sense of these forecasts is to see how they measure up against both past performance and industry growth estimates. We would highlight that sales are expected to reverse, with a forecast 70% annualised revenue decline to the end of 2027. That is a notable change from historical growth of 85% over the last year. By contrast, our data suggests that other companies (with analyst coverage) in the same industry are forecast to see their revenue grow 21% annually for the foreseeable future. So although its revenues are forecast to shrink, this cloud does not come with a silver lining - Crescent Biopharma is expected to lag the wider industry.

The Bottom Line

The most important thing to take away is that analysts increased their loss per share estimates for next year. Regrettably, they also downgraded their revenue estimates, and the latest forecasts imply the business will grow sales slower than the wider market. Given the serious cut to next year's outlook, it's clear that analysts have turned more bearish on Crescent Biopharma, and we wouldn't blame shareholders for feeling a little more cautious themselves.
